title: Bubble: Towards Scalable Evolving Graph Processing via Mini-Batch Sorting
problem: Evolving graph processing on multicore systems suffers from cache contention and workload imbalance between threads, limiting scalability and performance despite increasing core counts.
motivation: Dynamic graphs (social networks, temporal networks, streaming graphs) require efficient ingestion and analytics. Existing systems (LSGraph, GraphOne, XPGraph) experience poor scalability due to contention and load imbalance.
method: When adding edges to a graph on multicore computers, processor cores interfere with each other accessing shared cache memory, and work becomes unbalanced between cores, which slows the system down. Bubble fixes this by sorting incoming edges in small batches (mini-batches) before adding them to the graph — this sorting groups related edges together so each core accesses only its own private L3 cache without interfering with others. As a result, adding new edges to the graph scales nearly linearly with more cores (gets faster proportionally), and the system still performs well when analyzing the graph afterward.
key_novelty: Mini-batch sorting arranges incoming edges so each processor core works only with its private L3 cache (built-in fast processor memory), eliminating the cache interference that limits multicore graph processing.
contributions: Bubble graph processing engine with mini-batch sorting
Cache-aware data layout exploiting private core caches
2.46x-8.86x higher ingestion throughput than LSGraph, GraphOne, XPGraph
0.77x-3.29x performance for graph analytics vs. state-of-the-art
limitations: CPU-only focus; specific processor architecture not detailed; analytics performance sometimes lower (0.77x baseline); limited to evolving graphs
primary_theme: Scalable Evolving Graph Processing via Cache-Aware Mini-Batch Sorting
